doctrine: Cold outreach is math layered on trust. Math: high-volume targeted sends measured by reply rate, filtered through qualification, converted on calls. Trust: every touchpoint must prove relevance in 5 seconds. Infrastructure (domains, DNS, warming, reputation) is the moat. Sell outcomes not deliverables (more jobs, more trust, more clients). Volume creates data, data creates clarity. 3-email max per sequence: Email 1 (value prop + relevance), Email 2 (proof/angle), Email 3 (low-friction close or exit). Gap Selling core: diagnose problem first, help prospect see the distance between current state (facts, problems, impact) and future state (desired outcome) - that gap is the deal value. COMBO prospecting: multi-channel (LinkedIn connection + comment + email sequence + phone call) beats single channel. Day 1 LinkedIn connect (no pitch), Day 2 email (visual gap), Day 3 LinkedIn comment, Day 4 email (competitor angle), Day 5-6 phone call, Day 7 email (easy exit). Trigger events (funding, job postings, rebrands, mergers, office moves) increase conversion 3-5x. Front-end offers (free audit, spec work, ambient audits, teardowns) earn attention before full pitch. ICP Waterfall: Tier 0 (triggered signal - recently funded, job posted, redesigned), Tier 1 (fit but no trigger), Tier 2 (broad TAM). Manual sourcing beats scraped lists. Local service businesses use Google Maps + Yelp over Apollo/ZoomInfo. Email rules: 2-4 word lowercase subject lines, under 80 words, one CTA, casual tone, send Tue-Thu 7-9:30 AM prospect timezone, thread follow-ups. Operator playbook: Week 1 infrastructure, Week 2 target list (75-100 hand-verified), Week 3 launch campaign, Week 4 measure, Month 2 add channels, Month 2-3 introduce front-end offers, Month 3+ scale winners. Domain architecture: minimum 5 lookalike domains, 2-3 inboxes per domain, 70/30 Outlook/Google split, cap 30 emails/inbox/day. DNS: SPF, DKIM, DMARC required. Warm 14-21 days before sending. Verify all emails, randomize send times, rotate copy, monitor bounces weekly (flag >3%), keep warmup continuous. Gap Selling 9 Truths: no problem = no sale, all sales involve change and emotion (logic justifies, emotion decides), customers dislike change, closer to decision = more alarm, gap size determines deal value, asking 'why' drives discovery, future state must be better than current state, nobody cares about you/product (only their problem), cost of staying same must exceed cost of changing.

prompts: Email 1 subject (2-4 words, lowercase, curiosity): 'your website' or 'quick question' or '[firstName], one thing I noticed'
Email 1 body: Name specific visual/operational gap observed, state what you do, ask if worth conversation, under 80 words
Email 2 (competitor angle): Reference 2-3 competitors in their space, add use case or social proof, under 80 words
Email 3 (easy exit): Low pressure, permission to say no, 'if this isn't priority, no worries; if you want to move forward, happy to help'
Discovery call opening: 'Walk me through how you're handling X right now'
Discovery call impact probe: 'What happens when a prospect sees those outdated photos? How does that affect your close rate?'
Discovery call gap quantification: 'What would it be worth to you if every prospect who visited your site saw a team that looked like they belonged on Fast Company cover?'

operating_rules: Math + Trust: high volume targeted sends (math) measured by reply rate, filtered through qualification, converted on calls (trust through relevance in first 5 seconds)
Outcome framing: sell 'more jobs' / 'more trust' / 'more clients' never 'SEO' or 'photography services'
Infrastructure is the moat: 50 healthy domains + clean waterfall beats better copy + 2 burned domains
3-email maximum per sequence: Email 1 (value prop + relevance), Email 2 (proof/angle), Email 3 (easy exit); if no response, move on
Never pitch before discovery: diagnose problem, quantify gap, paint future state, then present solution
Multi-channel > single-channel: prospect sees name in LinkedIn feed + inbox + hears voice on phone = cold stranger becomes trusted familiar presence
Tier 0 prioritization: recently funded / job posted / redesigned website / new executive hire / competitor rebrand = 3-5x higher conversion than cold with no trigger
Manual sourcing > scraped lists: hand-verified 75-100 leads with 1 specific problem noted per lead beats database scrapes
Domain hygiene: minimum 5 lookalike domains (.co, .io, .info variations), 2-3 inboxes per domain, 70/30 Outlook/Google split, 30 emails max per inbox per day
Warm 14-21 days before sending: use dedicated warming tool, monitor bounce rates weekly (flag >3%), keep warmup continuous
Copy rules: 2-4 word lowercase subject lines, under 80 words per email, casual tone (like texting professional acquaintance), one CTA per email, thread follow-ups under original subject
Send timing: Tuesday-Thursday, 7-9:30 AM prospect local timezone, randomize send times, rotate copy via spintax to avoid template fatigue
Front-end offers reduce friction: pitch free audit / spec work / ambient audit / teardown before full engagement to earn 10 minutes of attention
Gap is the deal: current state (facts, problems, impact) + future state (desired outcome) = gap = deal value; small gap = small deal, big gap = big deal
Customers dislike change: as they get closer to decision, alarm bells ring; cost of staying same must exceed cost of changing
Sales are emotional: logic justifies emotion decides; connect to how problem makes them feel, not just logical case

Trigger events: new funding (budget + need to look professional), new executive hire (wants to stamp mark), office move (new photos), competitor rebrand (pressure signal), job posting for marketing role (investing in brand), merger/acquisition (team unification)

weird_gold: Permission to say no increases reply rates: Email 3 paradox of explicitly telling prospect 'no worries if not priority' produces higher engagement than aggressive closing
Casual copy beats polished: lowercase subject lines, abbreviations, no formal greetings, template-phobic tone converts more than professional templates
Warming is not one-time: must run continuously even on active inboxes (counterintuitive but deliverability rule)
Zero triggers = 5x worse conversion: triggered (recently funded) outreach converts 3-5x higher than cold with no signal, not 10-20% better, but 300-500% multiplier
Manual 75-100 leads > millions of scraped names: hand-verified list with 1 specific problem noted per prospect beats enterprise database + ML targeting (data quality > volume for initial campaign)
Ambient audits: creating 5-second proof video (animate their static team photo) sent unprompted is higher-converting front-end offer than traditional audit/proposal
Emotion + math: 'What happens if you don't fix this?' generates 'yes' more than 'here's your ROI' (asking why triggers internal motivation discovery, not external case-building)
